title: The gap that counts as an outlier against the market and the last value is not stated, and no S1 rule package carries it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E4-003 (AC1, Data, Test cases); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.3.2 and A2.3.3.1 (VR-S1-003-1, BR-S1-003); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-16 to R-DIS-18, R-DIL-09, R-DIL-12); Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md T3.1, T3.2, T8; _work/msr/context/S1.md
section: RWB-S1-E4003-APP s3 Preconditions, s4 step 4, s8 BR1 and BR2, s13 Configuration; RWB-S1-E4003-CON s2, s8 BR5, s12.1
description: FEAT-VAL-03 and REQ-S1-002 require the new value to be compared with the market and with the last value and the gap flagged for a person, and FSD S1 A2.3.3.1 BR-S1-003 forbids any value a business person may change from being written in code, but no source in the set gives the size of the gap that counts as an outlier, its unit, its comparator or the rule id that settles it. R-DIS-16 names 'the valuation agent outlier check' and R-DIS-17 to R-DIS-18 test outlier_flag without a value, and TSD S1 T8 traces every S1 requirement to FEAT-VAL-01 with the story written 'one epic ahead', so no rule row is published for this step. The S1 rule package is Phase 2 and no S1 rule is in force, so a build that hard-codes a percentage or a distance would break BR-S1-003 openly. The story therefore reads the limit as a versioned reference-data row or rule row and, where the row or its rule cannot be resolved, flags nothing and records the rule gap (X6).
evidence: FSD S1 A2.3.3.1 VR-S1-003-1 'Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status)'; BR-S1-003 'No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-16 'Record the value and run the valuation agent outlier check', R-DIS-17 'outlier_flag = N or officer_accepted = Y', R-DIS-18 'officer_accepted = N'; TSD S1 T8 rows 'Written one epic ahead'; no row of LOV-APPRAISAL or LOV-ROUTE gives a limit.
owner_role: Business owner of S1 Valuation and route, with the rule owner of rwb-decision
proposed: Hold the gap limit, its unit and its comparator as one versioned reference-data row of rwb-case with its valid-from date, and the rule that settles the outlier as a row of the S1 rule package; the step reads both with their version, flagging nothing and recording the rule gap where either is absent. The business owner names the values before the wave 3 entry gate.

title: The market value has no published owner, operation or element, and the model gateway the FSD names is not a contract of this service
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.3.2 (integration points 'ACE (v_ace_valuation; SVAF ingested by ACE), Model gateway') and A2.3.1; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml /cases/{caseId}/route, RouteRequest and Approval; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-VAL-03 (systems 'SVAF, Model gateway'); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-20; _work/msr/context/S1.md ownership rows (no event, no table, no job)
section: RWB-S1-E4003-APP s2, s3, s4 step 4, s5 X4, s11, s12.2, s19; RWB-S1-E4003-CON s3, s8 BR2, s12.2, s12.8
description: The FSD and the feature sheet name a Model gateway as the system behind the market value, and nothing else: no owner, no operation, no path, no element, no version and no freshness rule is published for the benchmark anywhere in the source set. The published route operation carries RouteRequest (route, override reason code, note) and Approval (decision, level, amount, status) and no market element, so the benchmark cannot be read as an element of an existing contract either. Under Arch v5 the model gateway is the agent runtime of rwb-agent (P10) and its contract is DP-20, which the plan does not carry for this story; the pattern set of the legacy key is DP-03, DP-05, DP-13 and DP-19. The story therefore declares the benchmark as an input element of the step with its source and its date, makes no model call of its own, and records the path where the benchmark is absent. Two readings are open and the pack does not settle them: the benchmark arrives on the rwb-source-data data product, or it arrives on an rwb-agent contract read by this service.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.3.2 'Integration points. ACE (v_ace_valuation; SVAF ingested by ACE), Model gateway'; Epics 3 to 8 Specification row FEAT-VAL-03 systems 'SVAF, Model gateway'; API Specification v4 'Approval' properties id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount, status and no market element; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-20 'Agent client | rwb-agent contract | C RWB-P10-TE013-CON'; split_plan.json slice RWB-S1-E4003-APP patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 and C [].
owner_role: Solution architect of S1 with the owner of rwb-agent (P10) and the owner of rwb-source-data (P1)
proposed: Declare the market benchmark as an input element of the outlier step, with its source name, its source date and its version, carried on whichever contract publishes it first; keep the placeholder and no path until one owner publishes it, and do not add a DP-20 dependency to this legacy key unless the agent contract is chosen as the route.

title: The previous value the new value is compared with is not defined by any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E4-003 AC1 and Data; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.3.2 and A2.4.3.2 field catalog; Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md T3.1 (valuation), T3.3
section: RWB-S1-E4003-APP s2, s3, s4 step 5, s5 X5, s8 BR3, s11
description: The legacy criterion compares the new value with 'the previous value', and no source says which previous value that is: the latest prior appraisal of the same asset on `v_ace_valuation`, the last accepted value in `valuation_ext` (accepted = Y), the value the route band was last fixed on, or the asset value on the books. FEAT-VAL-02 links each appraisal to the asset by business key and FEAT-VAL-04 accepts a value and fixes the band on it, so both readings are supported by the module, and R-DIS-17 updates the appraised value after an acceptance without naming the comparison basis. Because the comparison is what the flag is made of, the choice changes the outcome of the check and cannot be left to the build.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-003 AC1 'compares the new value to the market and the previous value and flags the gap for a person'; FSD S1 A2.3.2 'Compares the new value to the market and the previous value and flags the gap for a person'; FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 field catalog rows for v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext with no prior-value field; TSD S1 T3.1 'valuation' with one appraisal row per record and no predecessor.
owner_role: Business owner of S1 Valuation and route
proposed: Take the previous value as the latest prior appraisal of the same asset_key on the data product, record that basis and its date on every flag, and switch the basis to the last accepted value of valuation_ext if the business owner prefers it; the choice then changes one read and the recorded basis, not the shape of the baseline.

title: Where the outlier flag and the two gaps are stored is not fixed: the Ownership Map gives S1 no table while TSD S1 declares one
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md ownership rows (tables 0, 'None'); Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md T3.0 and T3.1 (`valuation` NEW, DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043, DF-COL-044); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.4.3.2 (`valuation_ext`); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-17 (outlier_flag)
section: RWB-S1-E4003-APP s3, s9, s11, s12.7, s13 Database and migrations; RWB-S1-E4003-CON s3, s11, s12.7
description: The Ownership Map row for S1 declares no table at all, and the context pack repeats it: tables 0, 'None'. TSD S1 T3.1 declares `valuation` as a NEW Workbench table with the appraisal fields, `accepted`, `stale_flag` and `age_days`, and FSD S1 holds the acceptance in a Workbench-owned `recovery.valuation_ext`, while the routing logic of asset disposal reads a column named outlier_flag. No source places the flag, its reasons or the two gaps in any of those objects, and the two gaps are elements this realignment adds because the comparison feeds them to the record and the screen. The story therefore computes both gaps per check, records them in the local decision record through the library of DP-03, and declares no table and no column of its own until the data owner of the service names the store.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S1.md '### Tables (0) - None'; TSD S1 T3.1 '**valuation** (NEW). An appraisal of collateral or an asset.' with DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043 stale_flag and DF-COL-044 age_days and no outlier column; FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 'valuation_ext.valuer_partner_id ... with the acceptance in recovery.valuation_ext'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-17 'outlier_flag = N or officer_accepted = Y'.
owner_role: Data owner of rwb-valuation with the owner of the ACE DB epics (RWB-PLT-DB)
proposed: Keep the flag and the two gaps in the local decision record for wave 3 and let the data owner decide whether `valuation` in rwb_valuation or `valuation_ext` carries a persisted copy; the DB story of the service then adds the column in its own Flyway sequence and the contract baseline declares the element in a minor version.

title: The names of the consumed operations of the outlier step are not published, and the plan carries no contract dependency for them
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (service row, ownership rows, naming rules); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (no source-data, decision or reference-data operation for this step); Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md T5.2 ('Calls go through the published Java interfaces'); split_plan.json slice RWB-S1-E4003-APP (C [])
description: The step consumes six rows of five owners: the rwb-source-data data product that carries the appraisal, the acceptance and the previous value, the market benchmark, the gap rule of rwb-case reference data, the rwb-case case state, the rwb-decision rule in force and the rwb-access authorise call. Only the case read (`GET /cases/{caseId}` family) and `POST /authorise` have a published shape; the other four are named in the FSD, the TSD and the case screen states but no operation, path, parameter or element is published for them, and the plan gives this slice an empty contract-dependency list. The baseline and the build therefore declare each row with its owner, its use, one hop and a 2 s budget, carry the placeholder where the name is not published, and build against fakes on Day 1.
evidence: Context pack S1 ownership rows list three REST operations provided and no consumed row; API Specification v4 carries no source-data, decision or reference-data path; TSD S1 T5.2 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data'; split_plan.json RWB-S1-E4003-APP C [] and X [].
owner_role: Owners of rwb-source-data (P1), rwb-case (P3), rwb-decision (P7) and rwb-access (P4), with the tech lead of rwb-valuation
proposed: Publish the four consumed operations on the owners' bases with their names and elements before the wave 3 entry gate; until then the baseline keeps the placeholder and no path, the build runs on the documented fakes, and the C dependencies of this slice are recorded as missing rather than as absent by design.

title: No source names the trigger that starts the outlier check, and the ownership rows give S1 no job and no event
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.3.2 ('Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-16 (valuer reported) and R-UNI-37; _work/msr/context/S1.md ownership rows (events 0, jobs 0); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E4-003 AC1 ('When its trigger arrives')
description: The legacy criterion says only 'When its trigger arrives'. FSD S1 A2.3.2 names three possible triggers in one phrase, a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, without choosing one or naming it, R-DIS-16 has the check run when the valuer reports the value, and R-UNI-37 re-runs the gates after an upstream correction. The ownership rows of the service give it no event and no job, so no subscription, no Schedule and no queue can be declared, and a batch-completion trigger would need a row the map does not carry. The story therefore runs the check as a step of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` when the route assessment reaches it and on the re-assessment that follows a new or corrected value, and declares no subscription and no Schedule.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.3.2 step 1 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; context pack S1 '### Events (0) - None' and '### Jobs (0) - None'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-16 'VALUER_REPORTED | Any | Record the value and run the valuation agent outlier check' and R-UNI-37 'UPSTREAM_DATA_CORRECTED ... Recompute the segment and re-run the gates'.
owner_role: Solution architect of S1 with the owner of rwb-case (P3) for the stage signal and the owner of rwb-decision (P7) for the rule version
proposed: Start the check from the value step of RouteDecisionWorkflow and from the re-assessment that follows a new or corrected appraisal; if a valuer-report event is wanted later, it is a new event of the owner that publishes it and a new story of this service, not an unnamed subscription of this one.

title: The outlier element of the route answer is in no published schema, and the approved answer carries only the approval elements
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml /cases/{caseId}/route (RouteRequest: route, overrideReasonCode, note; Approval: id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount, status); Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md T-A.2 (Request RouteRequest, Response Approval) and T3.1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md A2.3 and A2.4
description: The step's outcome has to reach the person who accepts the value, and the only operation of this key is the route decision, whose published answer `Approval` carries an id, a case, a decision, a preparer, a level, an amount and a status, and no appraisal, market, gap or flag element. No schema, no example and no OpenAPI component names the outlier element, its nested elements, its types or its nullability, and the FSD describes the outcome only in words ('flags the gap for a person'). The contract baseline therefore needs one additive element, and a name for it, that no source publishes: it declares the element under a draft name marked as not published, carrying the two gaps, the flag, its reasons, the threshold version and the rule version, and keeps every published element unchanged.
evidence: API Specification v4 'Approval' properties id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount, status, with no appraisal or outlier property; TSD S1 T-A.2 'Request | RouteRequest' and 'Response | Approval'; no `outlier` match anywhere in the API Specification v4 extract; FSD S1 A2.3.2 'flags the gap for a person' with no element list.
owner_role: Solution architect of S1 with the owner of the edge contract (RWB-PLT-N001) and the API owner
proposed: Declare the outlier element as an additive optional element of `Approval` under a draft name, keep its elements typed and nullable, and let the API owner rename it at the tag without a major version while no consumer is released; publish the shape in the S1 API file of the specification suite.
